_meta.source: Written for claudeDM (Horror category). Original content; a few general-mechanics sentences (opportunity attacks, death saves, conditions) are adapted from SRD 5.1, licensed CC BY 4.0 — see NOTICE.
_meta.notes: Gear for Horror campaigns in the 1890s, 1920s and 1970s, era-tagged; each item has one 'cost' string giving the period price, by era where it differs. Ammunition is recorded on character sheets as a counted equipment line named by the weapon's ammo_name in equipment.json, such as ".38 rounds (18)", ".30 cartridges (20)", "Shotgun shells (10)" or "Arrows (20)", and deducted shot by shot (combat.json ammunition); each ammo_name has a box here named "<ammo_name> (N)". Items with 'uses' are consumables, recorded with a count, e.g. "Salt (1 lb) (2)", "Candle (6)". The wards and rites items are ordinary objects: they matter only where a creature's rules say they do (dread.json rites_and_wards). Vehicle statistics are in combat.json vehicles. Medical items implement the no-magic healing rules in combat.json healing.

gear.name: Candle
gear.description: A tallow or wax candle. Dim light in a 10-ft radius for 1 hour (dread.json light_and_dark). A draught, a fall or a breath puts it out. Record as "Candle (6)".

gear.name: Lantern
gear.description: A tin kerosene lantern with a glass chimney. Bright light in a 30-ft radius and dim light 30 ft beyond for 6 hours on a pint of kerosene. Dropped or struck (AC 12), it breaks and spills burning oil in a 5-ft square (combat.json fire). Can be shuttered to a single beam, or to dark, as a free interaction.

gear.name: Kerosene (pint)
gear.description: A pint of lamp oil in a tin: one filling for a lantern (6 hours). Poured out and lit, it burns a 5-ft square for 1 minute; bottled with a rag, it is a Kerosene bottle (equipment.json). Record as "Kerosene (pint) (2)".

gear.name: Flashlight
gear.description: An electric hand light. In the 1970s: bright light in a 60-ft cone and dim light 60 ft beyond for 4 hours on a set of batteries. In the 1920s: dim light only in a 30-ft cone for 2 hours, and it flickers. Dropped, it rolls; it does not break on a 1-15 on a d20.

gear.name: Batteries
gear.description: One set of dry cells for a flashlight (4 hours in the 1970s, 2 in the 1920s) or a portable radio or tape recorder (8 hours). Record as "Batteries (2)". Cold halves their life.

gear.name: Matches (box)
gear.description: Fifty strike-anywhere matches, or a book of paper matches in the 1970s. A struck match gives dim light in a 5-ft radius for one round. Striking one in wind, rain or with shaking hands (Dread 3 or higher) takes a DC 10 DEX check.

gear.name: Salt (1 lb)
gear.description: Coarse kitchen or rock salt. A pound lays an unbroken line across one doorway or window, or a ring 10 ft across around one or two people. A line works only against a creature whose rules say salt bars it (dread.json rites_and_wards), and only while it is unbroken: a draught, a dog, a careless foot or a mop ends it. Record as "Salt (1 lb) (2)".

gear.name: Iron nails (box)
gear.description: Fifty cut or forged iron nails. Driven into a door frame, a windowsill, a coffin lid or a grave, they are a ward against a creature whose rules say iron bars or binds it. A handful thrown at a spirit vulnerable to iron is an improvised ranged attack (1d4 piercing, iron).

gear.name: Chalk
gear.description: A stick of white chalk. Marks walls, floors and doors: a way out, a warning, a sign a creature's rules say it must respect, or a line to show whether something crossed it in the night.

gear.name: Holy water (vial)
gear.description: A vial of water blessed by a clergyman of some faith, or taken from a font. It is water. What it does depends entirely on the creature: if a creature's rules say blessed water harms or bars it, it does (a thrown vial is an improvised ranged attack, 2d6 damage to such a creature and nothing to anything else); otherwise it makes things wet. Record as "Holy water (vial) (2)".

gear.name: Family Bible
gear.description: A heavy family Bible, or the holy book of another faith, with births, marriages and deaths written in the front by several generations. As a book it is a comfort (dread.json recovery). As a record it is often the best evidence of who was born, who married whom and who died when, sometimes better than the county's (Research).

gear.name: Rosary or prayer beads
gear.description: A string of beads for counting prayers, of whatever tradition the carrier keeps. Holding it and praying is a fitting way to recover Dread once per day (dread.json recovery). Against a creature it is only beads, unless that creature's own rules say otherwise.

gear.name: Hand mirror
gear.description: A small glass mirror. Lets you look around a corner or behind you. Some things do not show in a mirror, some show as they really are, and some cannot bear to see themselves; a creature's rules say which.

gear.name: Silver coin
gear.description: A silver dollar or an old silver piece. Pressed against a creature vulnerable to silver it is an improvised melee attack (1d4 bludgeoning, silver); laid on a threshold or under a tongue it may matter, if a creature's rules say so. A jeweller or a smith can make it into silver tips or rounds in a day.

gear.name: Silver tips (6)
gear.description: Six silver arrowheads or bolt points, made to order. Fitting them takes a short rest; record the tipped shafts separately, e.g. "Arrows (14)" and "Silver-tipped arrows (6)". A silver-tipped shaft counts as silver (combat.json fighting_the_supernatural). Recovered on a 1-3 on a d6 after a fight.

gear.name: Silver rounds (6)
gear.description: Six cartridges cast with silver bullets for one calibre, by a gunsmith who did not ask why. They fire as that calibre but count as silver; they are a little less accurate (no change on the sheet; the GM may call a miss on a natural 2). Record them separately from ordinary ammunition with the calibre named, e.g. "Silver .38 rounds (6)", and say which you load when you reload.

gear.name: Rope (50 ft)
gear.description: Hemp rope (nylon in the 1970s). Holds 500 lb. Tie off before going down a well, a cliff or a cellar ladder; a party roped together in fog or a burning building can't be separated without someone choosing to cut it.

gear.name: Crowbar
gear.description: An iron pry bar. Advantage on STR checks to force a door, a shutter, a crate, a grave slab or a coffin lid. It is also a weapon (equipment.json Crowbar); write it in the weapons list if it is carried to fight with.

gear.name: Shovel
gear.description: A spade. Digging a grave down to the coffin takes two people about two hours (one person four), less in sandy soil, more in clay or frozen ground. A swung shovel is an improvised weapon (1d4 bludgeoning; the blade is steel, not iron).

gear.name: Lock picks
gear.description: Picks and tension wrenches. Proficiency adds your proficiency bonus to Mechanics checks to pick locks. A house door lock is DC 12, a good safe-deposit or vault lock DC 18, an old crypt padlock DC 10 (and loud). Carrying them is a crime in most towns.

gear.name: Tool kit
gear.description: Screwdrivers, wrenches, pliers, a hammer, wire, tape and fuses in a canvas roll or a metal box. Needed for most Mechanics checks to repair an engine, a generator, a radio, a telephone line or a lighthouse clockwork; proficiency adds your proficiency bonus to them.

gear.name: Magnifying glass
gear.description: A good lens. Advantage on Investigation checks to examine small things closely: handwriting, a stain, a scratch, a hair, an engraving worn nearly smooth. It can also light a fire in strong sun.

gear.name: Field glasses
gear.description: Binoculars. Things far off are seen as if ten times nearer. Useless in the dark; a light in a far window or a figure on a dark field can still be picked out.

gear.name: Notebook and pencil
gear.description: For dates, names, rubbings of gravestones and the rules you think the thing follows. Players whose characters write things down may ask the GM to repeat what they recorded.

gear.name: Playing cards
gear.description: A deck of cards: solitaire on a long night, a game to keep the household calm, a fortune-teller's spread, or a stage medium's props. Proficiency adds your proficiency bonus to Sleight of Hand checks with them.

gear.name: Box camera
gear.description: A wooden box camera with a roll of film for a dozen exposures, developed by mail or at a studio in a week, or in a day in a city. It needs daylight or flash powder (an action, a blinding flash in a 20-ft radius, and smoke). Some things show on a photograph that did not show to the eye; some things never show at all (a creature's rules say which).

gear.name: Folding camera
gear.description: A compact bellows camera with film for eight exposures; flashbulbs ($0.10 each) light a room for an instant. Developed at a drugstore in two or three days. As the box camera, photographs may show what the eye missed.

gear.name: Instant camera
gear.description: A camera that develops its own prints in about a minute; a pack of film makes ten pictures ($5), and the flash cube lights four. A picture of an empty room that comes up with someone in it is the first fear check of a long night.

gear.name: Tape recorder
gear.description: A battery cassette recorder with a built-in microphone, eight hours on a set of batteries and an hour on each cassette ($2). Records interviews, and sometimes voices in empty rooms that were not heard at the time (a creature's rules say which).

gear.name: CB radio
gear.cost: $90 (1970s), plus a car or a truck to put it in
gear.description: A citizens-band transceiver in a car or truck, with a range of a few miles (more at night, less in hills). Anyone with a CB on the same channel hears you, including truckers, the sheriff's office, and people in town you would rather did not. A storm, a cut antenna, or the thing itself can fill the channel with static.

gear.name: Telephone call
gear.cost: $0.10 local, $1-$3 long distance (1890s, from the exchange or a hotel) / $0.05 local, $1 long distance (1920s) / $0.10 local, $0.50 a minute long distance (1970s)
gear.description: In the 1890s, telephones are in town: the exchange, the doctor, the hotel, a few rich houses. By the 1920s most towns and many farms have a party line, which means the neighbors listen. By the 1970s nearly every house has a phone. Lines can be cut, and a small exchange operator hears everything (dread.json isolation).

gear.name: Telegram (per word)
gear.description: Sent from the telegraph office at the railroad depot or the post office; ten words is the minimum charge. Arrives the same day. The telegraph operator reads every word, and in a small town so does everyone the operator talks to.

gear.name: Newspaper
gear.description: Today's local paper: obituaries, the shipping news, who visited whom, a short paragraph about a stranger who has not been seen since Tuesday. Back issues are in the newspaper's morgue or the library (dread.json investigation).

gear.name: Library card
gear.cost: Free, or $1 a year for a subscription library
gear.description: Lets you borrow books and use the reading room of a town or college library, and ask the librarian, who knows more about the town than anyone suspects. Rare books and local history collections may need a letter as well.

gear.name: Doctor's bag
gear.description: Scalpels, forceps, needle and suture, bandages, antiseptic (carbolic in the 1890s), a stethoscope, a few drugs of the period. Required for the Physician's Steady Hands. Gives advantage on Medicine checks to stabilize; proficiency adds your proficiency bonus to Medicine checks to treat wounds. 10 uses; refilled at a pharmacy or a hospital.

gear.name: Bandage roll
gear.description: Clean gauze or linen strips. One use ends Bleeding on a creature without a check. Record as "Bandage roll (4)".

gear.name: First-aid kit
gear.description: A tin box of bandages, iodine or antiseptic, tape, aspirin and burn salve. Advantage on a Medicine check to stabilize a creature or treat a burn, 5 uses.

gear.name: Smelling salts
gear.description: A vial of ammonia salts. As an action, wake a creature that has fainted or been knocked out (not one at 0 HP and dying), or give a creature at Breaking point a moment's clarity: it can choose its route out of the scene (dread.json dread). 5 uses.

gear.name: Laudanum (bottle)
gear.description: Tincture of opium, sold over the counter by any druggist in the 1890s as a period fact: for pain, coughs and sleep. A dose gives 1d6 + 2 temporary hit points for 1 hour, but the creature is poisoned for that hour and can't take a reaction; a second dose within 8 hours risks unconsciousness (DC 13 CON save). It does not lower Dread; it only dulls everything else. 6 doses.

gear.name: Whiskey (bottle)
gear.description: A bottle of rye or bourbon (or something worse during Prohibition, 1920-1933). A drink with company is a fitting way to recover 1 Dread once per day (dread.json recovery); more than one is disadvantage on DEX and WIS checks for an hour. Ten drinks.

gear.name: Coffee (1 lb)
gear.description: Ground coffee, or a thermos of it already made in the 1920s and 1970s. A night watch with coffee has advantage on its first CON save against falling asleep. A pound makes about forty cups.

gear.name: Cigarettes
gear.description: A packet of twenty (hand-rolled in the 1890s, with a pouch of tobacco). Sharing one in the dark is a fitting way to recover 1 Dread once per day (dread.json recovery). A lit cigarette gives no useful light but can be seen across a field.

gear.name: A few good books
gear.description: Two or three volumes chosen by the owner: a novel, a book of poems, a field guide or a history of the county. Reading by a lamp on a long night is a comfort; the history may be useful (Research).

gear.name: Good suit or dress
gear.description: Clothes fit for a reading of a will, a funeral, a dinner with the old families, or an interview at the bank. Without them, persuading the propertied is at disadvantage.

gear.name: Work clothes
gear.description: Overalls, denim, flannel, sturdy boots. Right for a barn, a dig, an engine or a field at night. Wrong for a parlor.

gear.name: Oilskins
gear.description: A waterproof slicker and hat. Advantage on CON saves against cold when wet, at sea or in a storm; a lantern carried under it stays lit in the rain.

gear.name: Bedroll
gear.description: Blankets and a ground sheet. Sleeping out in cold without one gives no long rest.

gear.name: Train ticket (per 100 miles)
gear.description: Coach fare. The 1890s and 1920s are the age of rail: almost every town has a depot and two trains a day. By the 1970s many branch lines are closed and the bus takes the passengers; the last bus out may be tomorrow (dread.json isolation).

gear.name: Boat passage
gear.description: A seat on a ferry, a mail boat or a fishing boat going your way. Island and river boats run on a schedule, and on the weather; the last boat of the day leaves before dark (dread.json isolation).

gear.name: Hotel room (night)
gear.description: A room at the hotel, the boarding house or a roadside motel. A long rest in a locked, lit room in town is the safest rest there is (dread.json recovery), unless the thing is in the town.

gear.name: Meal
gear.description: A hot plate at a diner, a boarding-house table or a church supper. The cook and the waitress know everyone in town.

gear.name: .32 rounds (50)
gear.description: Cartridges for the Pocket revolver. Record as ".32 rounds (N)".

gear.name: .38 rounds (50)
gear.description: Cartridges for the Service revolver. Record as ".38 rounds (N)".

gear.name: .45 rounds (50)
gear.description: Cartridges for the .45 automatic. A spare magazine (holds 7) is $2 / $10; filling one takes a minute. Record as ".45 rounds (N)".

gear.name: Flares (6)
gear.description: Signal flare cartridges for the Flare pistol, in a waterproof tin. Record as "Flares (N)".

gear.name: .30 cartridges (20)
gear.description: Rifle cartridges for the Lever-action rifle. Record as ".30 cartridges (N)".

gear.name: Rifle cartridges (20)
gear.description: Full-power cartridges for the Hunting rifle. They do not fit the Lever-action rifle. Record as "Rifle cartridges (N)".

gear.name: Shotgun shells (25)
gear.description: Twelve-gauge buckshot for both shotguns. Record as "Shotgun shells (N)". Birdshot (same price) deals 1d8 less but still scatters.

gear.name: Crossbow bolts (20)
gear.description: Bolts for the Crossbow. Recovered on a 1-3 on a d6 after a fight if you can search for them. Record as "Crossbow bolts (N)".

gear.name: Arrows (20)
gear.description: Hunting arrows for the Hunting bow. Recovered on a 1-3 on a d6 after a fight. Record as "Arrows (N)".
